question_stem: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 12 ohms are connected in PARALLEL across an ideal 8 V DC battery. What is the total current drawn from the battery?

subject: Reasoning Ability
subtopic: Coded Inequalities — Complementary Either-Or vs Strict Sign
question_stem:
Statement: P >= Q = R >= S (Step 1)
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. P = S
option_a: Either Conclusion I or II follows
option_b: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
option_d: Both Conclusions I and II follow
misconception_label: Marking "Neither" on a Valid >= Split (Either > or =)
why_trap_is_wrong: From P >= Q = R >= S, the combined relation is P >= S. Individually neither P > S nor P = S is 100% certain, so candidates mistakenly pick "Neither", forgetting they form an Either-Or pair!
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Trace the chain from P to S: does EVERY link allow equality (=), or is there at least one strict ">" sign?
fast_exam_shortcut: Chain P >= S splits into (P > S OR P = S) -> Either I or II follows.

subtopic: Percentage Base-Shift Trap ("A is X% more than B" => "B is ?% less than A")
question_stem: In a bank zone audit, Branch A processed 240 loan files while Branch B processed 200 loan files (so Branch A processed 20% more files than Branch B). By what percentage is Branch B's count LESS than Branch A's count?
misconception_label: Symmetric Percentage Base Error (Assuming +X% More Implies -X% Less)
why_trap_is_wrong: "More than B" divides the gap (40) by B (200), whereas "less than A" divides the same gap by the larger denominator A (240), giving 16.67%, never 20%.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Look at the word after "than": "less than Branch A" puts Branch A (240) in the denominator!

subtopic: Logarithms & AM-GM Minimum Value
question_stem: For real numbers x > 1 and y > 1, what is the minimum possible value of 2 * log_x(y) + 8 * log_y(x)?
misconception_label: Symmetric x = y Substitution Trap Instead of Term-Equality in AM-GM
why_trap_is_wrong: Plugging x = y gives log_x(y) = 1 and yields 2 + 8 = 10. In AM >= GM, equality holds when the TWO TERMS are equal (2t = 8/t => t = 2), giving 8.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Let t = log_x(y) > 0, so log_y(x) = 1/t. Apply AM >= GM to the positive sum (2t + 8/t).
fast_exam_shortcut: With t = log_x(y) > 0: 2t + 8/t >= 2 * sqrt(2 * 8) = 2 * 4 = 8 (attained at y = x^2).

subject: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension (VARC)
subtopic: Critical Reasoning — Confounding Variable vs Extreme Scope Trap
question_stem:
Editorial (2020 Case #1): "Districts that adopted remote work policies recorded a 18% improvement in software patent filings within two years. Therefore, remote work policies alone is sufficient to drive software patent filings."
Which finding, if true, most seriously undermines the editorial's conclusion?
option_a: Implementing remote work policies required a modest administrative training budget in year one.
option_b: Not every individual participant in those districts personally preferred remote work policies in post-pilot surveys.
option_c: Adjacent countries have debated remote work policies in parliamentary committees over the past decade.
option_d: Every district selected to pilot remote work policies simultaneously received expanded R&D tax credits during the exact same two-year window.
misconception_label: Subjective-Sentiment Distractor vs True Causal Confounder
why_trap_is_wrong: Participant survey sentiment does not explain why the measured 18% shift in software patent filings occurred; introducing simultaneous expanded R&D tax credits directly breaks the causal attribution to remote work policies.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Identify the causal leap: Correlation (remote work policies + 18% shift) -> Sole Cause. Which option introduces a simultaneous second cause?
fast_exam_shortcut: Correlation-to-causation weakener template: find the bundled co-intervention (expanded R&D tax credits) that explains the 18% change.

question_stem:

option_b: Implementing high-speed rail corridors required a modest administrative training budget in year one.

in_test_ai_hint_level1: Identify the causal leap: Correlation (high-speed rail corridors + 29% shift) -> Sole Cause. Which option introduces a simultaneous second cause?
fast_exam_shortcut: Correlation-to-causation weakener template: find the bundled co-intervention (state seed-capital grants) that explains the 29% change.

subtopic: Indian Polity — No-Confidence Motion vs Censure Motion (Drill Variant 1)
question_stem: [Prelims Concept Check #1] With reference to parliamentary motions in India, which statement accurately distinguishes a No-Confidence Motion from a Censure Motion?
option_a: A No-Confidence Motion can be moved against an individual Union Minister in either House of Parliament.
option_b: A No-Confidence Motion can be moved ONLY in the Lok Sabha against the entire Council of Ministers without stating specific reasons for its adoption.
option_c: Passage of a Censure Motion in Lok Sabha makes resignation of the Council of Ministers constitutionally mandatory under Article 75.
option_d: The Constitution of India explicitly uses the phrase "No-Confidence Motion" in Article 75(3).
misconception_label: Individual Minister & Article 75 Textual Trap
why_trap_is_wrong: Collective responsibility under Art. 75(3) is to the House of the People (Lok Sabha) as a whole; Rule 198 of Lok Sabha Rules (not Art. 75 text) governs No-Confidence Motions, and they apply only to the entire Council, never one minister.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Check Article 75(3): to which single House is the Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
fast_exam_shortcut: No-Confidence = Lok Sabha ONLY + Entire Council + No reason needed + Rule 198 (phrase absent in Constitution text).

subject: General Studies Paper I
subtopic: Indian Economy — RBI Open Market Operations & Liquidity (Drill Variant 1)
question_stem: [Prelims Concept Check #2] When the Reserve Bank of India conducts an outright SALE of Government Securities (G-Secs) under Open Market Operations (OMO), what is the immediate monetary effect?
option_a: Rupee liquidity is absorbed from the banking system, putting upward pressure on short-term bond yields.
option_b: Rupee liquidity is injected into commercial banks, lowering bond yields.
option_c: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) mandate is automatically reduced by an equal percentage.
option_d: India’s fiscal deficit shrinks by the face value of the securities sold by RBI.
misconception_label: Buyer-vs-Seller Cash-Flow Direction Reversal Trap
why_trap_is_wrong: Students see "Sale of G-Secs" and think money enters the market. When RBI SELLS bonds, banks pay rupees TO the RBI in exchange for paper, draining systemic rupee liquidity.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Follow the rupees, not the paper: if RBI hands G-Sec paper to banks, which way do the rupees flow?
fast_exam_shortcut: RBI Sells Bonds => Banks pay Rupees to RBI => Liquidity SUCKED OUT => Bond prices fall => Yields RISE.

question_stem: [Prelims Concept Check #37] When the Reserve Bank of India conducts an outright SALE of Government Securities (G-Secs) under Open Market Operations (OMO), what is the immediate monetary effect?
option_a: Rupee liquidity is injected into commercial banks, lowering bond yields.
option_b: Rupee liquidity is absorbed from the banking system, putting upward pressure on short-term bond yields.
option_c: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) mandate is automatically reduced by an equal percentage.
option_d: India’s fiscal deficit shrinks by the face value of the securities sold by RBI.
misconception_label: Buyer-vs-Seller Cash-Flow Direction Reversal Trap
why_trap_is_wrong: Students see "Sale of G-Secs" and think money enters the market. When RBI SELLS bonds, banks pay rupees TO the RBI in exchange for paper, draining systemic rupee liquidity.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Follow the rupees, not the paper: if RBI hands G-Sec paper to banks, which way do the rupees flow?
fast_exam_shortcut: RBI Sells Bonds => Banks pay Rupees to RBI => Liquidity SUCKED OUT => Bond prices fall => Yields RISE.

question_stem: [Prelims Concept Check #40] Why are winter "Western Disturbances" arriving over northwestern India crucial to Indian agriculture?
option_a: They are tropical cyclones steered westward by Trade Winds across the Arabian Sea.
option_b: They originate in the Bay of Bengal during retreating monsoon and irrigate Kharif paddy across Punjab and Haryana.
option_c: They occur exclusively between June and August during the peak Southwest Monsoon.
option_d: They originate as extratropical cyclones over the Mediterranean region, carried eastward by the Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream, providing vital winter rain for Rabi wheat.
misconception_label: Direction-of-Name Trap ("Western" Misread as West-Moving Tropical Storm)
why_trap_is_wrong: Meteorological winds are named by the direction they COME FROM: "Western Disturbances" come FROM the west (Mediterranean -> Iran -> NW India) and nourish winter Rabi crops, not Kharif paddy.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: In meteorology, a "westerly" comes FROM the west. Which winter crop is growing in Punjab/Haryana in January?
fast_exam_shortcut: Western Disturbance = Mediterranean extratropical storm + Westerly Jet + Winter rain (Mahawat) -> Rabi Wheat.

question_stem: [Prelims Concept Check #41] With reference to parliamentary motions in India, which statement accurately distinguishes a No-Confidence Motion from a Censure Motion?
option_a: A No-Confidence Motion can be moved against an individual Union Minister in either House of Parliament.
option_b: A No-Confidence Motion can be moved ONLY in the Lok Sabha against the entire Council of Ministers without stating specific reasons for its adoption.
option_c: Passage of a Censure Motion in Lok Sabha makes resignation of the Council of Ministers constitutionally mandatory under Article 75.
option_d: The Constitution of India explicitly uses the phrase "No-Confidence Motion" in Article 75(3).
misconception_label: Individual Minister & Article 75 Textual Trap
why_trap_is_wrong: Collective responsibility under Art. 75(3) is to the House of the People (Lok Sabha) as a whole; Rule 198 of Lok Sabha Rules (not Art. 75 text) governs No-Confidence Motions, and they apply only to the entire Council, never one minister.
in_test_ai_hint_level1: Check Article 75(3): to which single House is the Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
fast_exam_shortcut: No-Confidence = Lok Sabha ONLY + Entire Council + No reason needed + Rule 198 (phrase absent in Constitution text).
